items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Let me put my name on here. I'm Dick Allen.

ctx.x: My name is William Risley. During my music career, I was better known as Bebe Risley. I lived in 907 Edinburgh Street. I first played bass violin, then I played trombone, and I played drum. And so I lost my health.

Let me put my name on here. I'm Dick Allen. Okay. He wanted to ask you some questions about trombone playing. He just was asking you one, so I thought we'd better get the machine on before you explain too much. Ask him the question again.

The question, Risley, I've had this formal education in playing trombone in concert bands, in marching bands. But I'm always playing set notes of music, something that somebody else has written for me. And I'm very enchanted by this Dixieland music where the trombone player seems to be making it up and improvising and playing things that aren't written. And the music is a very happy type of music, which I think is good for relaxation for lawyers, among other people. And I'm wondering, how do you play, what do you…
